content.text:
**Scope:** The diff covers soft delete, plus an edit route, the article list limit, and the `editedAt` marker. I checked the two questions you asked, then the other rules the diff touches. Rule values come from the team notes in your task. The notes are not in this working directory, so I did not read them from disk. I did not run the tests or the migrations, since there is no database here.

## Answers to the questions

**Q1. What happens on delete, and which comments appear in lists?**
Answer: the row is kept, `deletedAt` is set, and comments with `deletedAt` set are left out of lists. Only the author may delete.
Source: `policy-soft-delete`. `code-comment-model` says deletion removes the row today. That describes the baseline, which this change replaces, so it is not a conflict.

| Check | Code (file:line) | Rule value and source | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delete sets `deletedAt` | `article.service.ts:564-571` calls `update` with `deletedAt: new Date()` | Set `deletedAt`, keep row (`policy-soft-delete`) | PASS |
| Row not removed | `article.service.ts:564`: no `prisma.comment.delete` call left | Keep row (`policy-soft-delete`) | PASS |
| Only author may delete | `article.service.ts:536-541`: lookup filters `author.id = userId` | Only author (`policy-soft-delete`); `code-comment-ownership` agrees | PASS |
| Deleted comments left out of lists | `article.service.ts:443-447`: `deletedAt: null` in `getCommentsByArticle` | Leave out (`policy-soft-delete`) | PASS |
| Other comment lists | Grep of `app/src`: `getCommentsByArticle` is the only comment list | Applies to all lists | PASS |

**Q2. Shape and status codes for API errors.**
Answer: `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. HTTP status codes do not change.

Two sources disagree:
- `policy-error-response` says every new error response uses the error object, and that it replaces the older errors-by-field body.
- `ops-runbook` says new error responses should follow the `errors` key shape, `{"errors":{"body":[...]}}`.

I followed `policy-error-response`. It is the rule written for this change and it names the older shape as replaced. The runbook describes how support reads failures, so it probably needs updating. Until it is, support tooling will miss the new error shape.

## Error paths in the diff

**FLAG 1.** `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts:579-580`, `editComment` blank body.
- Code: `HttpException(422, { errors: { body: ["can't be blank"] } })`. Old errors-by-field shape.
- Rule: error object shape (`policy-error-response`).
- Status 422 matches the convention in `code-error-shape`, and the rule keeps status codes, so the status passes.

**FLAG 2.** `article.service.ts:596`, `editComment` comment not found or not owned.
- Code: `HttpException(404, { errors: { comment: ['not found'] } })`. Old shape.
- Rule: error object shape (`policy-error-response`).
- Status 404 passes the same way.

**FLAG 3.** `article.service.ts:599-602`, edit window passed.
- Code: `throw new Error('the edit window for this comment has passed')`. `main.ts` answers `res.status(500).json(err.message)`, so the body is a bare string.
- Rule: error object shape (`policy-error-response`). The body fails it.
- Status: no rule sets a status for a refused edit. `policy-edit-window` says only that the API refuses the edit. The code comment at line 600 says the same, so I cannot check the 500 against a rule. A refusal returned as 500 is an open item for the rule owner, not a value I can confirm.

The new test `comment-edit.service.test.ts` checks the old `errors` shapes, so it locks in FLAG 1 and FLAG 2.

The existing 404 and 403 in `deleteComment` (lines 555, 559) are not new paths, so the error shape rule does not apply to them here.

## Other rules the diff touches

| Rule | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `policy-article-list-limit`: max 50, default 10 | `article.service.ts:69-88`: `Math.min(Number(query.limit) \|\| 10, 50)` | PASS |
| `policy-edit-window`: 30 minutes after creation | `article.service.ts:575, 599`: 30 × 60 × 1000 ms, refuses when elapsed is greater than the window | PASS. Exactly 30 minutes is allowed. |
| `policy-edit-window`: author only | `article.service.ts:582-586` filters `authorId: userId` | PASS |
| `policy-edited-at-marker`: nullable, null until first edit, set on edit | `schema.prisma` adds `editedAt DateTime?`. `article.service.ts:611` sets `editedAt: new Date()` | PASS |
| `policy-edited-at-marker`: migration does not change rows | `20261030120000_comment_edited_at/migration.sql`: `ADD COLUMN ... TIMESTAMP(3)`, nullable, no default | PASS |
| `policy-release-checklist`: one-line undo note per migration | Both new migrations begin with `-- Undo: ...` | PASS |
| `policy-release-checklist`: run `migrate deploy` on a fresh DB | Not run here, no database | NOT VERIFIED |

**Observation, not a flag:** `editComment` does not filter `deletedAt`, so a deleted comment can still be edited. The row stays out of lists. No rule covers edits to deleted comments, so I have not flagged it.

**Stale notes:** `code-comment-model` and `code-migrations` describe the baseline. The diff changes both, which is expected.

## Verdict

NOT APPROVED. The new `editComment` error paths at `article.service.ts:579-580` and `:596` use the old errors-by-field body, and the path at `:602` returns a bare string, not an error object. All three break `policy-error-response`. The 500 on the edit-window refusal also has no rule behind it.
